p: Bowling has a few unwritten rules that are worth sharing with the kids before the first ball goes down the lane. Wait for the bowler on the next lane to finish before you step up, never stray past the foul line onto the slippery bit, and keep drinks and snacks back at the seats rather than near the approach. Those hired shoes are for the lanes only, so swap back before nipping outside, and remember to hand them in at the end.

For beginners, a slow and steady roll is far better than a fast throw. Line up with the arrows rather than staring at the pins, and let the ball do the work. If a small child is struggling to lift a ball, a ramp lets them aim and push it down, and seeing those pins go flying gives them every bit as much of a thrill.
Why Clacton Works So Well for a Bowling Break

Having bowling right on the pier is a big plus in a resort where the day often hinges on the weather. You can keep a game up your sleeve for when the clouds roll in, or use it as a reward after a blustery walk along the beach. It's also handy for teenagers who have outgrown the soft play and want something to do that still feels a bit grown-up.

Clacton has been welcoming holidaymakers since Victorian times, and the pier dates back to 1871. Step off and you've got clifftop gardens, a long sandy beach and the town centre within easy walking distance. For a change of pace on another day, St Osyth, a few miles west, has a historic priory and a quieter stretch of coast.
